requirement: Describe the quantitative component as a prospective two-site, individually randomized, open-label, two-arm parallel study with 6 months of follow-up, embedded in a mixed-methods project.

evidence.text: The protocol describes a mixed-methods study, individual randomization at two shelter clinics and a six-month intervention/follow-up.

requirement: Define the experimental arm as hypertension-specific SMS support for medication and appointment adherence, lifestyle change and health education, and define the attention-control arm as general-health SMS content without hypertension-specific management; both arms also receive common phones, health education, welcome/birthday texts and routine appointment robocalls.

evidence.text: The protocol distinguishes hypertension-specific interactive SMS from general-health control SMS and lists shared education, phones, generic messages and robocalls.

requirement: Specify computer-assisted permuted-block randomization at the individual level, with block size four and stratification by the two clinic sites.

evidence.text: Participants are assigned by a computer-assisted permuted randomization schedule using blocks of four stratified by clinic site.

requirement: Define the participant population as English- or Spanish-speaking adults aged at least 21 years experiencing homelessness, receiving care at a participating shelter clinic, already diagnosed with hypertension and having most-recent-clinic SBP above 140 mmHg or DBP above 90 mmHg, subject to the stated pregnancy, recent cardiovascular-event, renal, SMS-use, mental-health, substance-use and consent exclusions.
acceptable_values: SBP above 140 or DBP above 90 mmHg

evidence.text: The protocol lists the target population, uncontrolled-BP threshold, language and clinical exclusions.

requirement: Before finalization, define the complete analysis-visit schedule, allowable visit windows and the rule for selecting measurements when regular clinic visits do not occur exactly at the planned baseline, 2-month and 6-month times.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies baseline, a scheduled two-month follow-up and regular clinic measurements through six months but does not define all nominal visits or windows.

requirement: Treat change from baseline to 6 months in systolic blood pressure and change from baseline to 6 months in diastolic blood pressure as distinct primary blood-pressure outcomes, with INT-versus-control treatment effects reported for each.
acceptable_values: SBP change from baseline to 6 months
DBP change from baseline to 6 months

evidence.text: Aim 1 and H1 specify six-month changes in SBP and DBP and an intervention-control difference.
The reference identifies changes in SBP and DBP from baseline and an INT-versus-control analysis after six months.

requirement: Derive blood-pressure outcomes from clinic-nurse measurements obtained after five minutes of rest with the participant seated upright, right arm supported at heart level and an appropriate cuff; keep this outcome measurement distinct from the most recent clinic reading used to establish eligibility.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies clinic-nurse BP collection and uses the most recent clinic value for uncontrolled-hypertension eligibility.
The reference specifies posture, arm position, cuff fit and five-minute rest for outcome measurements.

requirement: Before finalization, define the Voils DOSE nonadherence endpoint, including instrument items, scoring, direction, aggregation across visits and the exact six-month comparison; do not infer the later registry dichotomization from the protocol.

evidence.text: The protocol names repeated Voils DOSE nonadherence assessments but gives no item-level scoring or longitudinal derivation.

requirement: Derive appointment adherence from medical records as the number and percentage of kept appointments among all scheduled appointments over six months, and compare it between randomized groups.

evidence.text: The protocol says appointment attendance is measured through medical records.
The reference defines appointment attendance as kept appointments divided by all scheduled appointments and calls for group comparison.

requirement: Summarize phone retention and SMS engagement as secondary outcomes, including the number or frequency of message exchanges and texts read and responded to, separately by randomized group.

evidence.text: The protocol lists phone retention and counts of texts read and answered as other outcomes.
The reference calls for group-specific message-exchange analysis as an engagement measure.

requirement: Use the prospective sample-size target of 120 participants, 60 per arm, based on 80% power for an 8-mmHg between-group difference with assumed SD 15 mmHg, two-sided alpha 0.05 and a two-sample t-test; do not replace it with later actual enrollment.

evidence.text: The protocol prospectively targets 120 participants, 60 per randomized group, and an 8-mmHg difference.
The reference supplies the 80% power, SD 15, alpha 0.05 and two-sample t-test assumptions.

notes: The task is prospective SAP generation; registry actual enrollment is not a substitute for the planned target. The reference says it is powered for outcomes of AIM 2 immediately before calculating power for mean blood pressure, so the aim label requires expert confirmation.

requirement: Use intention-to-treat as the primary analysis principle, retaining participants in their randomized INT or attention-control group.

evidence.text: The reference explicitly states that the primary statistical analysis is on an intention-to-treat basis.

requirement: Report arm-specific summaries and between-group differences in means or response rates with 95% confidence intervals, using two-sided 0.05 tests where inferential testing is prespecified.
acceptable_values: difference in means or response rates

evidence.text: The reference requires comparative summaries, differences in response rates or means, 95% confidence intervals and two-sided alpha 0.05.

requirement: Include an unadjusted two-sample t-test comparing randomized groups for six-month change from baseline in SBP and separately in DBP.

evidence.text: The reference specifies a two-sample t-test for between-group differences in SBP and DBP change after six months.

requirement: Include a longitudinal mixed-effects analysis with time, randomized group and time-by-group interaction, and report treatment effects at each prespecified time point.

evidence.text: The reference proposes a mixed-effects model and a time-by-randomized-group interaction to estimate effects at each time point.

requirement: Before finalization, designate one definitive primary model for each blood-pressure endpoint and prespecify its covariates and repeated-measure structure; distinguish the roles of the reference plan's t-test, mixed-effects model and conditional ANCOVA rather than treating them as interchangeable.

evidence.text: The reference names a t-test, mixed-effects model and ANCOVA if covariates are needed without assigning an unambiguous primary/supportive hierarchy.

requirement: Before finalization, specify one executable primary model for medication adherence, including outcome scale, link, visit structure, within-participant correlation and treatment effect; resolve the reference plan's unresolved choice among final-visit regression, GEE and multivariate ANOVA.

evidence.text: The reference alternately proposes final-assessment regression and GEE or multivariate ANOVA without a complete model specification.

requirement: Before finalization, prespecify the adjustment covariates using clinical or design justification and reject selection based solely on observed randomization imbalance or univariate statistical significance.

evidence.text: The reference proposes including variables if imbalanced after randomization or significant in univariate analysis, requiring expert correction before finalization.

requirement: Before finalization, define the treatment effect of interest for each primary outcome and specify handling of intervention discontinuation, loss or replacement of the study phone, nonreceipt or crossover of SMS content, medication changes, missed clinic visits and withdrawal.

evidence.text: The protocol anticipates phone replacement, nonresponse and dropout outreach but gives no estimand or analysis strategy for these intercurrent events.

requirement: Before finalization, define item-level and visit-level missingness rules, the primary missing-data assumption and at least one sensitivity analysis for incomplete blood-pressure, medication-adherence and appointment records; do not rely only on mixed-model validity under MAR.

evidence.text: The protocol says missing data will be reviewed but gives no inferential handling.
The reference proposes reporting missingness and notes that a mixed model implicitly handles MAR, but supplies no sensitivity analysis.

requirement: Before finalization, define the hierarchy or joint success rule across SBP, DBP, medication adherence and appointment attendance and specify multiplicity control or explicitly designate nonconfirmatory outcomes.
acceptable_values: endpoint hierarchy or joint success rule

evidence.text: The protocol calls BP, medication adherence and appointment attendance primary outcomes and states two hypotheses without a hierarchy.
The reference applies two-sided alpha 0.05 but gives no multiplicity adjustment or success rule across outcomes.

requirement: Before finalization, specify the interim-analysis timing, data reviewed, statistical purpose, decision authority, blinding safeguards, stopping rules and any impact on type-I-error control or final confidence intervals.

evidence.text: The protocol states only that an interim analysis will be performed.
The reference repeats that an interim analysis will occur but provides no operating rule or alpha consequences.

requirement: For Aim 2, preserve separate patient and provider qualitative perspectives and finalize sampling targets, stopping or saturation criteria, transcription and coding procedures, two-reviewer reconciliation, auditability and the rule for integrating qualitative themes with quantitative findings.

evidence.text: Aim 2 uses semi-structured interviews with patients and providers but does not specify sample size or saturation.

The reference specifies 8-10 open-ended questions, grounded-theory content analysis and two reviewers who independently code and reconcile themes, but leaves sampling, saturation and integration incomplete.

requirement: Before finalization, state whether adverse events, critical blood-pressure values, medication-side-effect messages or SMS/phone process failures will be analyzed and, if applicable, define the safety population, observation period, coding and arm-level summaries.

evidence.text: The protocol describes urgent evaluation for critical BP, medication-side-effect messages and phone/process issues but neither document defines a safety analysis.
